reading.title: Breakfast Time
reading.text: Every morning Dad gets up first. He switches on the kettle and puts bread in the toaster. When the toast pops up, he puts butter on it. I take milk from the fridge and pour it into my glass. At the weekend Mum bakes bread in the oven, and the whole house smells wonderful. After breakfast we load the dishwasher together. Our kitchen is small, but it is a happy place.

options: She bakes bread in the oven

listening.title: Our Kitchen
listening.script: We have a lot of machines in our kitchen. There is a gas cooker with a big oven, and a fridge with a small freezer at the top. Every evening Mum loads the dishwasher. On Saturdays she puts our clothes in the washing machine. My favourite machine is the toaster, because my toast always pops up at the right time. My grandfather boils the kettle for his green tea all day long.

reading.title: A Picnic by the River
reading.text: On Sunday we had a picnic by the river. Mum cut the bread with a bread knife, and I put cheese on it. We forgot the metal forks, so we used plastic forks for the salad. Dad stirred the tea with a spoon and added a teaspoon of sugar to his cup. My little brother ate his yoghurt with a spoon, but he got it on his nose! We all laughed. Then we took a walk and found a fork in the road.

listening.title: Grandma's Kitchen
listening.script: My grandma has a lot of old things in her kitchen. She still has a wooden spoon from her mother. She says a sharp knife is safer than a blunt one, because a blunt knife slips. At dinner she puts a knife and fork next to every plate. When she makes soup, she adds a tablespoon of oil. I like to help her stir the soup with the wooden spoon.

reading.title: Tidying Up
reading.text: Last Saturday I helped Mum tidy the kitchen. First I opened every cupboard and looked inside. Then we put the big pots on the bottom shelf. The glasses went on the top shelf because the little children cannot reach it. The cupboard near the cooker was almost bare, so Mum wrote a shopping list. After that, Dad put up a new shelf for the spices. It was a long job, but the kitchen looked great.

listening.title: My Bedroom Shelf
listening.script: I have a long shelf above my desk. On the shelf there are my favourite books and a small clock. My brother put it up last year with Dad. I keep my football cards on the bottom shelf and my school books on the top shelf. In the kitchen, the cupboard door is broken. Dad will fix it tomorrow.

reading.title: Pancake Sunday
reading.text: On Sunday morning Mum makes pancakes. She mixes the eggs, milk and flour in a big bowl. Then she heats a non-stick pan on the cooker and adds a little oil. I watch the first pancake turn golden. Dad makes a pot of tea, and we all sit down to eat. Afterwards I help to wash the pots and pans. Mum says that cooking is fun, but the washing-up is the hard part.

listening.title: Cooking with Grandpa
listening.script: Yesterday I cooked with my grandpa. He put a big pot of water on the cooker and waited until it boiled. Then we added rice. In a frying pan we cooked onions and carrots with a little oil. The pan was hot, so he told me to be careful. After lunch he gave me a small flowerpot with a tomato plant. I put it on the window.

reading.title: A Birthday Party
reading.text: It was my little sister's birthday. Mum put paper plates on the table, and Dad filled a big bowl with fruit. In the kitchen, Grandma mixed the cake in a large mixing bowl. Each child filled a plate with rice, salad and chicken. My cousin asked, "Can you pass the plate of bread?" I passed it to him. At the end, we all had a bowl of ice cream. Everybody sang happy birthday.

listening.title: A Quiet Dinner
listening.script: Last night we had a quiet dinner at home. Dad put a bowl of hot soup in front of each of us. Mum passed me a side plate with bread. My brother filled his dinner plate with potatoes and fish. After dinner, my sister washed the plates in a washing-up bowl. I dried them. I do not like the washing-up, but the kitchen was clean in ten minutes.

reading.title: Who Does the Dishes?
reading.text: In our family everybody has a job. My sister cooks on Mondays and I do the dishes. After dinner, I fill the sink with hot water and add a little washing-up liquid. My brother dries the dishes and puts them away in the cupboard. Last week the sink was blocked, and the water would not go down. Dad called a plumber, who fixed it in ten minutes. Now the kitchen is clean again, and nobody complains about the dishes.

listening.title: A Messy Kitchen
listening.script: On Sunday there was a pile of dirty dishes in the sink. My mum was tired, so I decided to help. I filled the sink with hot water and washed all the plates and cups. My little sister dried them with a tea towel. Then we put away the dishes together. Mum came into the kitchen and smiled. She said, "Thank you, my helpers!"
